ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a cone, with a pointed top, and the bottom is drawn as an ellipse with a dashed rear edge; a circular marble is located inside the cone, exactly touching between the two slanted sides of the cone and close to the bottom, indicating that the marble exactly fits in the lower part of the cone. Reasoning: Take a vertical cross-section through the axis of the cone. In this cross-section, the cone becomes an isosceles triangle, the marble becomes a circle, and because it "fits exactly", this circle is tangent to the two slanted sides and the base of the triangle, so it is the incircle of this triangle. The problem states that the slant height of the cone is equal to the diameter of the base; in the axial cross-section, the two equal legs are the slant height of the cone, and the base of the triangle is the diameter of the base of the cone. Therefore the three sides of the triangle are equal, and it is an equilateral triangle. The radius of the incircle of an equilateral triangle is equal to one third of the height, so the height of the cone = 3 × marble radius = 3 × 15 = 45 cm.

raw_record.question_text: A marble with radius $15\mathrm{~cm}$ fits exactly under a cone as shown in the diagram. The slant height of the cone is equal to the diameter of its base. What is the height of the cone in $\mathrm{cm}$?

method.method_draft: Use the axial cross-section of the cone. From the image, take a vertical slice through the cone’s axis: the cone becomes an isosceles triangle, and the marble appears as a circle tangent to the two slanted sides and to the base, so it is the incircle of that triangle. From the text, the marble radius is 15 cm and the cone’s slant height equals the diameter of its base. In the cross-section, the two equal sides are slant heights and the base is the base diameter, so all three sides of the triangle are equal; the triangle is equilateral. In an equilateral triangle, the inradius is one-third of the altitude. Therefore the cone height is 3 times the marble radius: 3 × 15 = 45 cm.

method.method_draft: Work with half of the axial cross-section. From the image, the marble is tangent inside the cone, so its cross-section is an incircle of the triangular cross-section. Let the cone base radius be R and height be h. From the text, the slant height equals the base diameter, so l = 2R. In the right triangle formed by the cone height, base radius, and slant height, h^2 + R^2 = l^2 = 4R^2, so h = R√3. Now use the incircle formula for the full axial triangle: area = r × semiperimeter. Its area is Rh, and its semiperimeter is (l + l + 2R)/2 = (2R + 2R + 2R)/2 = 3R. Thus r = area/semiperimeter = Rh/(3R) = h/3. Since r = 15, h = 45 cm.

考虑完整轴截面的等腰三角形，它的底边为 2R，两腰都是 l = 2R。因此半周长为 (2R + 2R + 2R)/2 = 3R。该三角形面积也等于 (1/2)(2R)h = Rh。内切圆半径 r 满足 面积 = r × 半周长，所以 Rh = r(3R)，因此 r = h/3。marble 半径为 15 cm，所以 15 = h/3，得到 h = 45 cm。
